course_position.stage_name: Solid B1+ to Low B2 Development

lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Organize a spoken viewpoint with claim, reason, example, contrast, and conclusion.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: Giving a short spoken opinion about prices, transport, media habits, or digital services.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Producing a compact low-B2 viewpoint that is easy to follow.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik prepare short spoken viewpoints about whether higher prices change everyday habits.

main_focus.name: structured viewpoint with claim, reason, example, contrast, conclusion
main_focus.description: Use a simple five-part structure to make a spoken opinion coherent without becoming too formal.
model_examples: Jag tycker att priser påverkar vardagen eftersom man måste prioritera mer.
Sammanfattningsvis är det viktigaste att hitta en realistisk balans.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use one clear claim, one reason, one example, one contrast, and one concluding phrase in the dialogue.

allowed_supporting_grammar: concession with även om if natural

vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use viewpoint-organization chunks that can transfer to many everyday opinion topics.

dialogue_shape.opening: A practical opinion topic about everyday prices or habits is introduced.
dialogue_shape.middle: They build a short viewpoint step by step and check that each part is clear.
dialogue_shape.ending: They deliver or agree on a compact final version of the viewpoint.

target_complexity.repetition: The production target should feel like spoken Swedish, not a memorized essay.

focus: the main claim about how prices affect habits
the example that makes the claim concrete
the conclusion that summarizes the viewpoint

sentence_focus: one sentence introducing a claim with min poäng är att
one sentence giving a reason with anledningen är att
one sentence giving an example with till exempel
one sentence adding contrast with samtidigt
